cards.explanation: The answer is False. The writer says they heard it, saw it with their own eyes, gazed upon it and touched it with their own hands (1 John 1:1). That's a front-row seat, friends, and I think he'd have been a little offended by the word secondhand.

The answer is that they testify to it and proclaim it. The writer says, “we have seen it and testified to it, and we proclaim to you the eternal life that was with the Father and was revealed to us.” They saw it, and then they spoke up about it. When you've seen something that big, friends, sitting on it is not really an option.

The answer is so the readers can have fellowship with them. The writer says, “We proclaim to you what we have seen and heard, so that you also may have fellowship with us.” (1 John 1:3). He's opening the door and inviting the readers in. He also says they write so that their joy may be complete (1 John 1:4).

The answer is True. The writer says, “And this fellowship of ours is with the Father and with His Son, Jesus Christ.” (1 John 1:3). Two names, and both are the very top of the list. You can't get better company than that, friends.
The answer is joy. The writer says, “We write these things so that our joy may be complete.” (1 John 1:4). Joy is the word he picks, bakers. It's a pretty good reason to pick up a pen.
The answer is True. The writer says, “God is light, and in Him there is no darkness at all.” (1 John 1:5). Notice the words “at all,” friends. He doesn't leave even a little dark corner.

The answer is that we lie and don't practice the truth. The writer says, “If we say we have fellowship with Him yet walk in the darkness, we lie and do not practice the truth.” (1 John 1:6). What we say and how we walk have to match, friends. Otherwise the words and the walk are telling two different stories.
The answer is the blood of Jesus His Son. The writer says, “…the blood of Jesus His Son cleanses us from all sin.” (1 John 1:7). Notice the words “all sin,” bakers. It's no partial clean-up.

The answer is False. The writer says, “…if we walk in the light as He is in the light, we have fellowship with one another…” (1 John 1:7). Walking in the light goes with fellowship, not with losing it. A good kitchen is better when it's full of people, friends.

The answer is ourselves. The writer says, “If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.” (1 John 1:8). The one who gets fooled is the one doing the saying, friends. Quite a plot twist.

The answer is False. The writer says, “If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” (1 John 1:9). No makeup work is listed, friends, and no payment plan either. He is faithful and just to forgive.

The answer is liar. The writer says, “If we say we have not sinned, we make Him out to be a liar, and His word is not in us.” (1 John 1:10). Saying we've never sinned puts us at odds with what God says, friends. That's a bad spot to bake yourself into.

The answer is Jesus Christ, the Righteous One. The writer says, “But if anyone does sin, we have an advocate before the Father—Jesus Christ, the Righteous One.” (1 John 2:1). An advocate is someone who stands up for you, friends. When we sin, we aren't left to speak for ourselves.

The answer is the whole world. The writer says Jesus “…is the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not only for ours but also for the sins of the whole world.” (1 John 2:2). That's a big reach, friends, and I can't think of a bigger circle to draw. It doesn't stop with the writer and his readers.
